t.E509.agn: In 2019, EFSA re-evaluated E 507, E 508, E 509 and E 511 together; it stated that acute toxicity was low and that there was no concern regarding genotoxicity or carcinogenicity, and used a reference value of 40 mg/kg body weight per day for chloride. It has been reported that this value may be slightly exceeded in high consumers in some age groups (toddlers, children, adolescents), but it was concluded that there was no safety concern at the reported use levels.
t.E509.body: In the gastrointestinal tract it dissociates into chloride and the accompanying ions. Chloride taken in with food is almost completely absorbed along the intestine and distributed to organs and tissues; the amount in the body is regulated by balance mechanisms, and it is excreted mainly in urine, and also in sweat and faeces.
t.E509.found.0: Canned and bottled fruit and vegetables
t.E509.found.2: May be used at quantum satis (as much as needed) in many foods in the EU
t.E509.prod: It may be obtained from natural mineral deposits or by chemical production.
t.E509.regx.0: Chlorides E 507–E 511 re-evaluated together; no safety concern at the reported use levels (reference for chloride 40 mg/kg bw per day).
t.E509.regx.1: Group I additive; also permitted at quantum satis in canned/bottled fruit and vegetables and in fruit compotes other than apple.
t.E509.summary: Calcium chloride. It firms the texture of canned vegetables and fruit and helps coagulation in cheese making.
t.E509.what: It is a mineral salt that regulates consistency and texture and helps keep fruit and vegetables firm. Chloride and calcium are natural minerals also taken in with food.
